subject.title: [Bug] Sandbox validateEnvVarValue base64 heuristic false-positives on legitimate long alphanumeric values

question: Should OpenClaw narrow sandbox env credential-data warnings to structured base64 values on credential-looking env names, accepting fewer warnings for neutral or nonstandard names?
rationale: The false positive is source-reproducible, but the proposed fix changes advisory sandbox credential-warning coverage, so automation should not choose the security tradeoff alone.

options.title: Approve narrow warning policy
options.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main, port the skill caller to `src/skills/runtime/env-overrides.ts`, and land the key-aware structured-base64 sanitizer if sandbox/security owners accept the reduced neutral-name warnings.

options.title: Preserve broader warning coverage
options.body: Keep this issue open and request a different heuristic that reduces false positives without requiring credential-like env names.

options.title: Close as intentional policy
options.body: If broad warnings are preferred for sandbox safety, close this issue as not planned and document that the warning is intentionally conservative.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow warning policy
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR onto current main, port the skill caller to `src/skills/runtime/env-overrides.ts`, and land the key-aware structured-base64 sanitizer if sandbox/security owners accept the reduced neutral-name warnings.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest history-backed owner for the sanitizer warning threshold and security-boundary policy choice.
